text:
Mika Chong: FYI Sparrow's account (POC) wants a 'pricing safety net' — 28% off list for months 1-6 if usage < 40% of committed. They're asking to bake it into the 12mo commit doc. Need deal desk + legal quick read.
Jason Patel: Sounds like a POC-to-prod ask. What's the committed baseline and expected ARR? Any dedicated capacity?
Mika Chong: Baseline is 200M token/mo commit (approx 60 RU). Expected ARR if converted: ~$240k/year. No Dedicated initially, but they want option to convert to Dedicated at month 7.
Emma Li: 28% is pretty steep. Quick thumb rule: we can entertain up to 15% off list on standard commits; anything >20% needs finance approval and an offset (e.g., shorter price-floor period or reserved capacity upsell).
Samir Kaur (Legal): We can draft a limited safety-net clause. Suggest: "If usage < X% for first Y months, customer eligible for one-time credit up to Z% of fees paid" — avoids open-ended rollback. Also need an explicit lookback window and notice period.
Nina Gomez: Can you drop exact numbers? If it's 28% credit vs 28% price reduction that's different for revenue recognition. Also need forecasted uplift to model margin impact. @Emma what's the minimum margin we should hold?
Emma Li: Minimum gross margin after concessions should be ~55% to approve without exec signoff. With a 28% reduction we'd be below that unless we get a firm conversion trigger to Dedicated or a minimum spend floor.
Ben Ortiz: From infra side, if they convert to Dedicated at month 7 we can reserve capacity but need a 45d lead time. Recommend adding an "opt-in to Dedicated" clause with committed start date to protect infra scheduling.
Olivia Park: Security check — no new controls needed for this ask. Standard SOC/KMS stuff still applies. No blocker from sec.
dealbot: Ticket #D-8731 created for pricing-exception; assignees: @EmmaLi @NinaGomez. SLA: 72h.
Jason Patel: Could we instead offer: 20% concession for months 1-3, then 10% for months 4-6, plus guaranteed conversion window to Dedicated with a 6mo min if they convert? That reduces revenue hit and gives them runway.
Mika Chong: That sounds reasonable. They want to keep the 'safety' language though — prefer predictable credits vs retro pricing changes.
Samir Kaur (Legal): Draft clause option A (credit): "If cumulative usage < 40% of committed over first 6 months, Redwood will issue a one-time credit equal to X% of fees paid for that period, capped at $Amount." Option B (true price floor) is riskier for revenue recognition. Recommend A.
Nina Gomez: If we go with Jason's tiered concession (20/10) + opt-in Dedicated trigger, finance can approve conditionally. Need final numbers to calc net present value. Put proposed floor caps in USD not just %.
Emma Li: Agree. Put a $50k cap on credits, 20% months 1-3, 10% months 4-6, Dedicated conversion clause with 6mo min commitment and 45d notice. That's within revops comfort.
Jason Patel: I'll run that by Sparrow now. @Mika can you confirm they'll accept the cap and the dedicated conversion term?
Mika Chong: Pinged them. They said cap is acceptable if Dedicated conversion window is guaranteed and pricing for Dedicated is locked for 12 months post-conversion. Asking for final legal wording and finance signoff.
Samir Kaur (Legal): I'll draft language this afternoon and post in the thread for sign-off.
Nina Gomez: Once Samir posts, I'll run the numbers and clear if margin >=55% with the caps. If not, escalate to @CTO for exec approval.
Ben Ortiz: Noted on the 45d lead — will block capacity once signed.
Mika Chong: Thanks everyone. Please tag when you post drafts/approvals so I can share with customer. :pray:
Jason Patel: Thanks — will update after Sparrow respond.
